value: more detections of individuals during daylight hours
method: passive acoustic telemetry (ten Vemco VR2W receivers on the northern reef slope of Heron Island Reef); detections compared among dawn (0400-0659), day, dusk (1700-1959) and night, with mean detections standardised to sentinel-tag mean detections per hour
conditions: Wild adult trumpet emperor captured by rod-and-reel line fishing on 22-23 March 2014, tagged, fork length recorded and released (release site not named), and tracked on a ten-receiver array on the northern reef slope of Heron Island Reef, southern Great Barrier Reef. Sample as printed: eleven fish tagged, seven detected over 93 days (22 March to 22 June 2014), five detected consistently and included in analyses; 'the other four individuals were excluded from the analysis because their detection profiles suggested they had perished' (the printed counts do not reconcile: seven detected, five retained, four excluded). The paper does not state which individuals or how many entered the time-of-day detection comparison, and reports no statistical test or figure for detections by period. The measure is acoustic detection counts within receiver range (presence at the array), not tracked activity; the sentinel-tag standardisation indicated absence during crepuscular and night periods was not an artefact of transmitter detectability. Contrary space-use result from the same fish: horizontal core areas and vertical areas of extent were significantly larger during crepuscular and night periods than during the day (Abstract; not filed as a diel value here). Both results are stated; fewer night detections at the array may accompany larger night-time space use.
